disclaimer: Reminder reference only — NOT legal authority. Season dates, zones, and limits are set annually and can change. Always verify current regulations with the South Carolina Department of Natural Resources before hunting or trapping.

sources.title: S.C. Code Title 50, Chapter 11 (Protection of Game), via scstatehouse.gov
sources.notes: Official SC Legislature code. § 50-11-2540: commercial trapping Dec 1–Mar 1; coyote trapping Dec 1–Mar 1 with year-round take by other lawful means; noncommercial private-land beaver trapping year-round (2022 amendment). § 50-11-120: small game seasons (raccoon/opossum Sept 15–Mar 15; fox Thanksgiving–Mar 1; beaver year-round). Fur-bearing animals defined at § 50-11-2400(a)-ish (red/gray fox, coyote, raccoon, opossum, muskrat, mink, skunk, otter, bobcat, weasel, beaver).

license_summary.trapping_license: A Trapping and Commercial Fur Harvest License plus a hunting license are required to trap during the trapping season; the license is also required to sell or trade furbearers taken during hunting season or to possess 6 or more furbearers or their pelts. Resident $25 / nonresident $200; expires June 30, 2027.
license_summary.landowner_permission: Written permission from the property owner is required to trap on land you do not own (§ 50-11-2430).
license_summary.private_land_note: On private land, an individual (or agent) may trap furbearing animals noncommercially with only a valid statewide hunting license during the established open hunting season; beaver may be trapped noncommercially on private land year-round (§ 50-11-2540, as amended 2022).

verification.confirmation_notes: S.C. Code Title 50, Chapter 11 read 2026-09-18 from the official SC Legislature site (scstatehouse.gov): § 50-11-2540 (trapping season, incl. 2022 amendments) and § 50-11-120 (small game seasons).
known_gaps: Bobcat hunting may fall under the general small-game season (Thanksgiving Day–Mar. 1) but was not verified — not modeled; only trapping is modeled for bobcat.

On private land, noncommercial trapping with a hunting license is allowed during the established open hunting season (§ 50-11-2540(A)); only the explicit year-round private-land beaver provision is modeled as an additional season.
Scientific names are standard taxonomy, not stated in SCDNR regulations.
